text: Meet Maya. She's three weeks into Marketing Ops, and her manager just asked: why did trial MQLs drop at the end of July? So she starts digging. Team chat: forty threads. A fifty-eight-minute meeting recording. The handbook page, edited twice. An old PDF on the drive that still says twenty-five points. The lead score field in the CRM. The dashboard. A merge request. Seven tools later, she's still not sure who decided what, or why.

She just asks. And she gets the whole story: the trial threshold went from twenty-five to thirty-one points. Rachel Kim and the team decided it in the July seventeenth Marketing Ops weekly. Here's what was said, and here's the merge request that put it in the handbook. Every sentence links back to the exact version it came from.
That works because everything's connected. Meetings, chat, docs, old files, CRM fields, metrics, dashboards: one versioned graph, on FalkorDB. So the answer isn't a search result. It's a path.

And if you're new, it's the fastest way in. Pick your area, and just ask. What changed recently? Who should I talk to? Which tools will I use? Don't know a word? Click it. Anything on the screen, you can ask about, in plain English.
Leads can look at one domain at a time. And every decision gets triaged: a business rule, a process, or a system change, and how big the impact really is. Worked out from the graph, not guessed.

When something changes, HandbookBrain reads the diff. Answers that relied on the old rule go stale, the owners hear about it, and one click shows the blast radius: every document, metric and owner it touches.
And when a meeting decides something nobody writes down, the agent drafts the update and sends it to the right owner. People just approve.
HandbookBrain. Everything your company knows, in one place. And still true tomorrow.
